# Suparedirect

> Suparedirect is a self-hosted dereferer (Node.js, Express, Docker). A link to https://your-host/?to=<url> loads a page sent with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer that forwards the visitor by script, so the destination gets no Referer header.

Run it with `docker run -p 3000:3000 halitsever/suparedirect:latest`. Redirect stats are kept in memory (last 500) and served without auth on /api/stats.

## Docs

- [Home](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/): what it does and when you need it
- [Getting started](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/guide/getting-started): Docker and from source

- [Stats dashboard](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/guide/dashboard): what the numbers mean
- [Self-hosting notes](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/guide/self-hosting): port, stats endpoint, TLS
- [The Referer header](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/guide/referer-header): what browsers send and how to hide it
- [Do you need a dereferer?](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/guide/noreferrer-referrer-policy): link attribute, header or dereferer
- [Dereferer services compared](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/guide/dereferer-alternatives): hosted vs self-hosted

## Tools

- [Anonymous link generator](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/link-generator/): builds ?to= links for your instance and tests the referrer they send

## Blog

- [All posts](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/)
- [strict-origin-when-cross-origin, explained](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/strict-origin-when-cross-origin): What the strict-origin-when-cross-origin referrer policy sends for each kind of request, why DevTools shows it next to failed requests, and how to change it.
- [rel="noopener noreferrer": what each part does](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/noopener-noreferrer): What rel="noopener" and rel="noreferrer" each do, why target="_blank" already implies noopener, and when noreferrer is worth adding to a link.
- [Referrer-Policy header: best practices and every value](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/referrer-policy-best-practices): Every Referrer-Policy value in one table, a recommended default, fallback syntax, and how to set the header in nginx, Apache, IIS web.config and Express.
- [Reading HTTP_REFERER in PHP and nginx](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/http-referer-php-nginx): How to read the Referer header as $_SERVER['HTTP_REFERER'] in PHP and $http_referer in nginx, why it is often empty, and why it cannot be trusted.
- [How URL redirects work: 301, 302, meta refresh and JavaScript](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/how-url-redirects-work): The four ways to redirect a URL, what each status code means, how Google reads them, and which Referer the destination gets, tested in headless Chrome.
- [Redirect services with the target URL in the path](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/redirect-service-url-in-path): Path-style redirect URLs put the target after a slash instead of in ?to=. How they differ, where they break, and how to add a path route to Suparedirect.
- [The Referer in an HTTP request: how to read and test it](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/referer-in-http-request): Where the Referer header sits in an HTTP request, how to see it in DevTools, send or fake it with curl, read it in JavaScript and check what a link sends.
- [How to hide the referrer URL when linking out](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/hide-referrer-url): Four ways to hide the referrer URL from the sites you link to: rel=noreferrer, a Referrer-Policy header, a meta tag, or a self-hosted dereferer link.
- [Meta refresh and the Referer header: what a second refresh changes](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/meta-refresh-referrer): We tested single and double meta refresh redirects in Chrome: which Referer each hop sends, why the refresh page becomes the referrer, and what really hides it.
- [Redirecting with JavaScript, and what the Back button does after](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/javascript-redirect): Redirect with JavaScript using location.href, assign or replace, tested in Chrome: which ones keep the page in history and why redirects during load differ.
- [Open redirects: why they are risky and how to lock one down](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/open-redirect): What an open redirect vulnerability is, how phishing uses it, OWASP's fixes with a tested Node.js allowlist, and why a dereferer is an open redirect by design.
- [Referer or referrer: which spelling goes where](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/referer-vs-referrer): Why the HTTP header is spelled Referer while Referrer-Policy, document.referrer and rel=noreferrer use two r's, and which spelling each server expects.
- [What rel nofollow tells search engines, and what it does not change](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/rel-nofollow): What rel=nofollow does for Google, when to use sponsored or ugc instead, and how it differs from noreferrer and noopener, which change the browser instead.
- [UTM parameters explained, and how they survive a hidden referrer](https://projects.halit.org/suparedirect/blog/utm-parameters): What UTM parameters are, the five Google Analytics reads, how they keep attribution when the Referer is hidden, and how to pass them through a redirect intact.
